wu: Flashcard Race: Students stand in two lines. Teacher shows a clothing flashcard (e.g., 'hat'). The first student in each line runs to the board, draws the item, and says 'It is a hat.'
wuAlt: TPR Simon Says: Teacher says 'Simon says touch your shoes' and students touch the correct clothing item on their bodies.
Memory Game: Students sit in a circle. Teacher says 'I am wearing a jacket' and each student adds one item, e.g., 'I am wearing a jacket and shoes.'
pres: Teacher wears a funny outfit (e.g., over-sized hat, mismatched shoes). Points to each item and says 'I am wearing a hat.' 'He is wearing a jacket.' Uses flashcards to drill 6 clothing items. Checks understanding by asking 'What am I wearing?' and students point.
presAlt: Storybook: Read 'The Mixed-Up Chameleon' but replace animals with clothing items. Teacher says 'He is wearing a dress.'
Realia Show: Teacher brings a bag of clothes. Students pull one out and say 'It is a __.'
prac: Pairwork: Students get a worksheet with 3 people. They take turns saying 'He is wearing trousers.' 'She is wearing a dress.' Teacher monitors and helps with pronunciation.
pracAlt: Bingo: Teacher calls out clothing items. Students cover the picture on their bingo card. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Flashcard Guess: Student picks a flashcard without showing. Others ask 'Is it a hat?' and they answer 'Yes/No.'
ls: Clothing Song: Students listen to 'What Are You Wearing?' and point to their own clothes. Then listen again and draw 3 items they hear in a notebook.
re: Clothing Relay: Students line up. Teacher whispers 'Run to the board and draw shoes.' First student draws and says 'Shoes!'
prod: Guess Who: Students take turns describing a classmate's outfit. 'He is wearing a blue jacket and a hat.' Others guess who it is.
rw: Paper Doll Dress-Up: Students get a paper doll and 6 clothing stickers. They dress the doll and write sentences like 'She is wearing a dress.'
st: Story: Read 'Elmer's New Clothes' by David McKee. Sing 'Goodbye Song' and give stickers. Line up for high-fives.
g: Teacher calls a clothing item. Students jump to the flashcard on the floor.
Student mimes wearing an item. Others guess 'He is wearing a jacket.'
Teacher says 'Find someone wearing shoes.' Students link arms.
Teacher says 'Draw a boy wearing a hat.' Students draw and check.
Teacher shows 3 flashcards. Students close eyes. Teacher removes one. Students say 'The hat is missing.'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 sentences about what their family member is wearing.
Support: Trace the words 'shoes', 'hat', 'dress' in their notebook.
hw: Cut out 5 clothes pictures from a magazine and stick them in a notebook. Write the word under each.
Draw a picture of yourself. Label 3 things you are wearing.
Ask your family 'What are you wearing?' and write 2 sentences.
tip: Use local context: Bring in a djellaba or gandora to compare with 'jacket' and 'dress'. Link to Green March or Independence Day by describing traditional festival clothes.
